reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the cited text supports it: Section 3.4(a) lets Sanofi exercise licence rights through its Affiliates without RevMed's consent, Section 3.4(c)(i) permits unrestricted subcontracting to Third Parties, and Section 3.4(b) allows multi-tier sublicensing with a reasonableness-qualified consent only for substantially all US rights.

Non-revocability and successor transfer are evidenced: Section 12.3(b) makes the Section 3.1 licences fully paid up, royalty free, perpetual and irrevocable on expiration, and Section 15.2(a)(ii) permits assignment without consent to a successor in an asset sale or merger/acquisition — matching the preferred position.
No redline or comment was proposed, which is correct for a compliant finding; deterministic checks (affiliate coverage, no at-will revocation) both pass and the paragraphs are unchanged.

The rationale properly relegates the minor points (Affiliates take rights via exercise/assignment mechanics rather than as named direct licensees; grant-back scope) to notes rather than deviations, consistent with the playbook's classification semantics.
